notes: Three rules in testing.md changed since 93873be and were graded against the text at db91c23: "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" and "Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`". The other four graded rules are unchanged and were graded to the standard of the 2026-10-21 grade files.

Grouping is decided by two sentences of testing.md. "A block that joins two functions (`describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2"`) no longer says which one a failure is about.": 0 of 5 runs violate. "Name each test by the behaviour it checks: `test "returns :ok"` states a return value most functions share, so a failure line names nothing": 0 of 5 runs violate. The first sentence, "Name a `describe` block after the function under test, or after a condition its tests share", allows the condition blocks all five runs wrote (opus-1 line 109 with setup [:subscribe_and_exit]; haiku-1 lines 141 and 187; haiku-2 line 139; sonnet-1 lines 147 and 183; sonnet-2 lines 136 and 165). Under the 93873be text these would have been violations in 5 of 5 runs, as they were in all five skill runs of 2026-10-21.

start_supervised is decided by testing.md: "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason.": 1 of 5 runs violate (haiku-1 line 135 asserts the failure with GenServer.start/2); sonnet-1 (lines 52-53) and sonnet-2 (lines 37-39) follow it; opus-1 and haiku-2 have no start-failure test. "a server that registers `__MODULE__` by default takes a test-specific name built from the context's module and test name, `Module.concat(context.module, context.test)`": 0 of 5 runs violate; all five name every server Module.concat(module, test), and sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 add a "NoMailer" segment for the failing start. start_link/1 called from a test: 0 of 5. Previous sweep: 2 of 5 skill runs violated this rule.

Concurrency is decided by testing.md: "`Process.register(self(), TestMailer)` and `Application.put_env(:notify, :test_pid, self())` make the test process a singleton, which forces `async: false`.": 0 of 5 runs violate. All five use async: true, start the Registry in setup_all with start_supervised!/1, and register the test process under "the server's test-specific name, built from the test's module and name". Registry key per run: opus-1 module and test name (line 27: Module.concat(module, test)); haiku-1 module and test name (line 28: Module.concat(context.module, context.test)); haiku-2 module and test name (line 33); sonnet-1 module and test name (line 27); sonnet-2 module and test name (line 28). No run keys by the test name alone, which all four runs of the 2026-10-21 check batch did when the text showed name: context.test. Previous sweep: 3 of 5 skill runs violated this rule.

Unchanged rule "Assert with patterns": sonnet-1 (lines 60-61 and 169-170) and sonnet-2 (lines 47-48) are graded violated for assert [pid] = ... followed by assert pid == self(), the same shape the 2026-10-21 check batch graded violated (its sonnet-2 lines 55-56), following the rule's first "Instead of" example and the case check's assert [^pid] = .... 2 of 5 runs.

Unchanged rule "Wait for messages, not for time": opus-1 awaits the subscriber's exit with stop_supervised!(Task) (line 136) instead of its own monitor; graded clean and the exit check met, because stop_supervised!/1 returns only after the test supervisor has seen the process exit and nothing sleeps or polls. Process.sleep(:infinity) in opus-1 line 132 and sonnet-2 line 138 is the body that keeps a subscriber alive, not a wait for work, so it is not counted against the rule or the no-sleep check.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs, 20 times each with random seeds; every run passed every time with no compiler warnings, and all five files pass mix format --check-formatted. Both haiku runs read SKILL.md and testing.md but not processes.md, so the expected-reads check is missed in 2 of 5 runs.
